{{Short description|Kofun period decorated kofun Kofuns in Japan}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Ōzuka Kofun | native_name =王塚古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = Round side of Ozuka Ancient Grave 5.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption =Ōzuka Kofun | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Ōzuka Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E|region:JP-40|display=inline, title}} | map_dot_label = | location = [[Keisen, Fukuoka]], [[Japan]] | region = [[Kyushu]] | type = [[Kofun]] | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = c.6th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (no facilities) | Historic Site = | website = <!-- {{URL|example.com}} --> | architectural_styles = | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|Special National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E}}}}}}
The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[bronze mirror]], a [[lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[Keisen Station]] on the [[JR Kyushu]] [[Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.
==See also== *[[List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)]] *[[Decorated kofun]]

==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>

These include a [[bronze mirror]], a [[lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>

It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[:en:Sarcophagus|Sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[:en:Sarcophagus|Sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.
==See also== *[[:en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)]] *[[Decorated kofun]]

==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[:en:Sarcophagus|Sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[:en:Sarcophagus|Sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[:en:Sarcophagus|Sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of [[:en:Keisen, Fukuoka| Keisen]], [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the [[:en:Sarcophagus|Sarcophagus]], and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, [[:en:Bracken|''warabi'']] patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of [[:en:Grave goods|Grave goods]] were recovered. These include a [[:en:Bronze mirror|Bronze mirror]], a [[:en:Lapis lazuli|Lapis lazuli]] tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1956 and are stored at the [[:en:Kyoto National Museum|Kyoto National Museum]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from [[:en:Keisen Station|Keisen Station]] on the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]] [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

{{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|Special National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E}}}}}}
The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Keisen, Fukuoka|en|Keisen, Fukuoka|WD=Q1206263|lt= Keisen}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the {{ill|Sarcophagus|en|Sarcophagus|WD=Q48634|lt=Sarcophagus}}, and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, {{ill|Bracken|en|Bracken|WD=Q258034|lt=''warabi''}} patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of {{ill|Grave goods|en|Grave goods|WD=Q1399692|lt=Grave goods}} were recovered. These include a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=Bronze mirror}}, a {{ill|Lapis lazuli|en|Lapis lazuli|WD=Q216798|lt=Lapis lazuli}} tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1956 and are stored at the {{ill|Kyoto National Museum|en|Kyoto National Museum|WD=Q147286|lt=Kyoto National Museum}}.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from {{ill|Keisen Station|en|Keisen Station|WD=Q6383854|lt=Keisen Station}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}} [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Ozuka Kofun (Keisen)]][[de:Ōzuka Kofun]][[en:Ōzuka Kofun]][[ja:王塚古墳]][[zh:王塚古墳]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[co:commons:Category:Ozuka Kofun (Keisen)]][[de:Ōzuka Kofun]][[en:Ōzuka Kofun]][[ja:王塚古墳]][[zh:王塚古墳]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Ozuka Kofun (Keisen)]][[de:Ōzuka Kofun]][[en:Ōzuka Kofun]][[ja:王塚古墳]][[zh:王塚古墳]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11572952]] Wikidata name: Ōzuka Kofun [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:43, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Kofun period decorated kofun Kofuns in Japan}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Ōzuka Kofun | native_name =王塚古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = File:Round side of Ozuka Ancient Grave 5.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption =Ōzuka Kofun | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Ōzuka Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{Coord|33.588763888889|N|130.66394444444|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_dot_label = | location = {{ill|Keisen|WD=Q1206263}} | region = [[Kyushu]] | type = [[Kofun]] | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = c.6th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (no facilities) | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles ={{ill|decorated kofun|WD=Q11626716}}; {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|Special National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E}}}}}}
The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Keisen, Fukuoka|en|Keisen, Fukuoka|WD=Q1206263|lt= Keisen}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the {{ill|Sarcophagus|en|Sarcophagus|WD=Q48634|lt=Sarcophagus}}, and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, {{ill|Bracken|en|Bracken|WD=Q258034|lt=''warabi''}} patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of {{ill|Grave goods|en|Grave goods|WD=Q1399692|lt=Grave goods}} were recovered. These include a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=Bronze mirror}}, a {{ill|Lapis lazuli|en|Lapis lazuli|WD=Q216798|lt=Lapis lazuli}} tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1956 and are stored at the {{ill|Kyoto National Museum|en|Kyoto National Museum|WD=Q147286|lt=Kyoto National Museum}}.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from {{ill|Keisen Station|en|Keisen Station|WD=Q6383854|lt=Keisen Station}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}} [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.
==See also== *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|en|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|WD=Q13641288|lt=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)}} *[[Decorated kofun]]

{{Short description|Kofun period decorated kofun Kofuns in Japan}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Ōzuka Kofun | native_name =王塚古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = File:Round side of Ozuka Ancient Grave 5.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption =Ōzuka Kofun | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Ōzuka Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{Coord|33.588763888889|N|130.66394444444|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_dot_label = | location = {{ill|Keisen|WD=Q1206263|1=Keisen, Fukuoka}} | region = [[Kyushu]] | type = [[Kofun]] | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = c.6th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (no facilities) | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles ={{ill|decorated kofun|WD=Q11626716|1=Decorated kofun}}; {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|Special National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E}}}}}}
The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Keisen, Fukuoka|en|Keisen, Fukuoka|WD=Q1206263|lt= Keisen|1=Keisen, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the {{ill|Sarcophagus|en|Sarcophagus|WD=Q48634|lt=Sarcophagus|1=Sarcophagus}}, and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, {{ill|Bracken|en|Bracken|WD=Q258034|lt=''warabi''|1=Bracken}} patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of {{ill|Grave goods|en|Grave goods|WD=Q1399692|lt=Grave goods|1=Grave goods}} were recovered. These include a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=Bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, a {{ill|Lapis lazuli|en|Lapis lazuli|WD=Q216798|lt=Lapis lazuli|1=Lapis lazuli}} tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1956 and are stored at the {{ill|Kyoto National Museum|en|Kyoto National Museum|WD=Q147286|lt=Kyoto National Museum|1=Kyoto National Museum}}.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from {{ill|Keisen Station|en|Keisen Station|WD=Q6383854|lt=Keisen Station|1=Keisen Station}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company|1=Kyushu Railway Company}} [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.
==See also== *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|en|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|WD=Q13641288|lt=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|1=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)}} *[[Decorated kofun]]

{{Short description|Kofun period decorated kofun Kofuns in Japan}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]] | name = Ōzuka Kofun | native_name =王塚古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = File:Round side of Ozuka Ancient Grave 5.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption =Ōzuka Kofun | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Ōzuka Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{Coord|33.588763888889|N|130.66394444444|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_dot_label = | location = {{ill|Keisen|WD=Q1206263|1=Keisen, Fukuoka}} | region = [[Kyushu]] | type = [[Kofun]] | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = c.6th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (no facilities) | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles ={{ill|decorated kofun|WD=Q11626716|1=Decorated kofun}}; {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|Special National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E}}}}}}
The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Keisen, Fukuoka|en|Keisen, Fukuoka|WD=Q1206263|lt= Keisen|1=Keisen, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=[[Zenpokoenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the {{ill|Sarcophagus|en|Sarcophagus|WD=Q48634|lt=Sarcophagus|1=Sarcophagus}}, and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, {{ill|Bracken|en|Bracken|WD=Q258034|lt=''warabi''|1=Bracken}} patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of {{ill|Grave goods|en|Grave goods|WD=Q1399692|lt=Grave goods|1=Grave goods}} were recovered. These include a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=Bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, a {{ill|Lapis lazuli|en|Lapis lazuli|WD=Q216798|lt=Lapis lazuli|1=Lapis lazuli}} tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1956 and are stored at the {{ill|Kyoto National Museum|en|Kyoto National Museum|WD=Q147286|lt=Kyoto National Museum|1=Kyoto National Museum}}.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from {{ill|Keisen Station|en|Keisen Station|WD=Q6383854|lt=Keisen Station|1=Keisen Station}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company|1=Kyushu Railway Company}} [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.
==See also== *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|en|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|WD=Q13641288|lt=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|1=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)}} *[[Decorated kofun]]

{{Short description|Kofun period decorated kofun Kofuns in Japan}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpōkōenfun]] | name = Ōzuka Kofun | native_name =王塚古墳 | native_name_lang = | image = File:Round side of Ozuka Ancient Grave 5.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption =Ōzuka Kofun | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = location in Japan | relief = 1 | map_caption = Ōzuka Kofun | map_size = 270px | altitude_m = | altitude_ref = | coordinates = {{Coord|33.588763888889|N|130.66394444444|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_dot_label = | location = {{ill|Keisen|WD=Q1206263|1=Keisen, Fukuoka}} | region = [[Kyushu]] | type = [[Kofun]] | part_of = | length = | width = | area = | volume = | diameter = | circumference = | height = | built = c.6th century | abandoned = | epochs =[[Kofun period]] | cultures = | discovered = | excavations = | archaeologists = | condition = | ownership = | management = | public_access = Yes (no facilities) | Historic Site = | website = | architectural_styles ={{ill|decorated kofun|WD=Q11626716|1=Decorated kofun}}; {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} | architectural_details = |notes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|[[Monuments of Japan|Special National Historic Site of Japan]]}} {{maplink2|type=point|frame=yes|plain=yes|zoom=14|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|35|19.55|N|130|39|50.2|E}}}}}}
The {{nihongo|'''Ōzuka Kofun'''|王塚古墳|}} is a [[Kofun period]] [[decorated kofun]] [[Kofun]]s, located in the Jumei neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Keisen, Fukuoka|en|Keisen, Fukuoka|WD=Q1206263|lt= Keisen|1=Keisen, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. The tumulus was designated a [[Monuments of Japan|National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1937, and elevated in status to that of a Special National Historic Site in 1956 <ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/173235|title=王塚古墳|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref>
==Overview== The Ōzuka Kofun was discovered by chance on September 30, 1934, when the front part of the stone [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] was scraped away during construction work. The shape of the tumulus is that of a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpōkōenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpōkōenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun|1=[[Zenpōkōenfun]]|2=前方後円墳|3=|4=}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above; however, more than half of the mound has been lost due to previous construction work. The original length is estimated to have been 86 meters, with a posterior circular portion diameter of 56 meters and height of 9.5 meters, and an anterior rectangular portion width of 60 meters. The tumulus was constructed in two tiers, with alternating layers of red and black clay, covered by ''[[fukiishi]]''. It was surrounded by a double moat.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=4311750404}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>
The burial chamber is a horizontal entry stone chamber, with a stone shelf at the top of the back wall and a small window above the entrance. It has a house-shaped cap stone that covers the {{ill|Sarcophagus|en|Sarcophagus|WD=Q48634|lt=Sarcophagus|1=Sarcophagus}}, and the floor is divided into areas for two burials, with two depressions are made to place the heads, and two stone pillows. However, it is estimated that four people were buried here. Currently, the [[:en:Burial chamber|Burial chamber]] is completely sealed for preservation, although it open to the public twice a year, in spring and fall. It is noteworthy in that mural painting that covers almost the entire surface of the burial chamber. The images depicted include horses, shields, swords, bows, and geometric patterns such as concentric ring patterns, {{ill|Bracken|en|Bracken|WD=Q258034|lt=''warabi''|1=Bracken}} patterns, triangular patterns, and circular patterns. Six colors (red, yellow, green, blue, black, and white) have been confirmed in [[decorated kofun]] around Japan, and this tumulus uses five of these six colors (except for blue). This is the highest number of colors for any known tomb in Japan.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
When [[archaeological excavation|excavated]], the burial chamber was found to be intact, and thus a large number of {{ill|Grave goods|en|Grave goods|WD=Q1399692|lt=Grave goods|1=Grave goods}} were recovered. These include a {{ill|Bronze mirror|en|Bronze mirror|WD=Q1041984|lt=Bronze mirror|1=Bronze mirror}}, a {{ill|Lapis lazuli|en|Lapis lazuli|WD=Q216798|lt=Lapis lazuli|1=Lapis lazuli}} tubular bead, two wooden beads with metal inlay, nine earthen beads, one amber bead, one gold item, metal fittings for horse harnesses, saddles and stirrups, and iron swords, arrowheads and a large quantity of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} pottery. The excavated artifacts were designated as a National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1956 and are stored at the {{ill|Kyoto National Museum|en|Kyoto National Museum|WD=Q147286|lt=Kyoto National Museum|1=Kyoto National Museum}}.<ref name="Shiseki"/>
The tumulus is a six-minute walk (480 meters) from {{ill|Keisen Station|en|Keisen Station|WD=Q6383854|lt=Keisen Station|1=Keisen Station}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company|1=Kyushu Railway Company}} [[:en:Chikuho Main Line|Chikuho Main Line]].<ref name="Shiseki"/>The {{nihongo|Ōzuka Decorated Kofun Museum|王塚装飾古墳館||}} on site has displays of the murals in the burial chamber.
==See also== *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|en|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|WD=Q13641288|lt=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)|1=List of Historic Sites of Japan (Fukuoka)}} *[[Decorated kofun]]
